options.plan: B2B Free; documented offer, no account entitlement verified
options.region: No tenant region selected; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: First-party public SPA/Native OIDC; code/S256 PKCE, token auth none, exact callbacks; no BFF, M2M, SCIM or brokers

conditions: Register separate first-party SPA and Native applications with Authorization Code enabled; verify token_endpoint_auth_method none for each public client rather than inferring it from the application-type label.
Use response_type code, openid scope and a fresh S256 PKCE verifier/challenge; validate issuer, state, nonce, ID-token signature and audience in the consuming application.
Configure narrowly registered callbacks and only required browser origins under https://auth0.com/docs/get-started/applications/application-settings; do not use production redirect wildcards.

The B2B Free offer at https://auth0.com/pricing is a scope reference, not tested account entitlement, a trial benefit or a future zero-cost guarantee; Cloud sources are mutable and dated, not release-pinned.
This scope excludes confidential BFF clients, M2M/API grants, third-party registrations, SAML, inbound SCIM and upstream enterprise brokers.

evidence.summary: The dated login guide describes Native/SPA registration, allowed callbacks, Authorization Code, S256 PKCE and openid scope for ID tokens. It proposes downstream OIDC login, not verified tenant configuration or Free entitlement.

conditions: Limit this proposal to a first-party public SPA using code/S256 PKCE and token authentication none; never ship a confidential client secret in browser code.
Enable at least one intended login connection for the SPA; configuring that connection does not establish enterprise SSO, SCIM or population/tenancy compatibility.
Test callback/origin policy, token storage and browser privacy restrictions independently; refresh-token rotation and local-session logout are not inferred from documented SPA registration.
Application registration does not prove deployment behavior or an implemented SDK; this scope is not AuthWeave's confidential Next.js BFF.

evidence.summary: The dated SPA guide describes a distinct browser application registration and enabling a login connection. Flow and application prerequisites remain explicit; no browser interoperability or session enforcement was tested.

conditions: Limit this proposal to a first-party public Native mobile OIDC client with code/S256 PKCE and token authentication none; register it separately from the SPA.
Application prerequisite: use an external user-agent under RFC 8252 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8252.html), not a credential-capturing embedded WebView.

Prefer claimed HTTPS Universal Links/App Links and verify platform association and callback ownership; PKCE alone does not prevent a malicious app from initiating its own login through a shared custom URI scheme.
If a non-verifiable callback is necessary, retain end-user confirmation and verify its actual behavior; a configured prompt is not evidence of verified callback ownership.
Test issuer/state/nonce, token storage and SDK integration independently; no mobile SDK, OS association, phishing-resistance control or local-session lifecycle was verified.

evidence.summary: The dated native-login guide describes code with PKCE, recommends claimed HTTPS callbacks and explains custom-scheme impersonation and conditional user confirmation. These are configuration prerequisites, not tested mobile assurance.
